passage: I am Avni, Jomon's big sister. In the toy shop our mother said no to the robot he wanted. Jomon's face went red and he stamped his foot. He crossed his arms and would not look at her. I could not tell what he felt exactly, but his chin shook like he was about to cry. Then he took a breath and said, "Can I have it on my birthday?" Mother smiled. "We can think about it then." He nodded and held her hand.

qa.q: What did Jomon ask his mother for at the end?
qa.a: He asked, "Can I have it on my birthday?"

qa.q: What might Jomon have been feeling when he crossed his arms and would not look at his mother?
qa.a: He seems furious and maybe hurt, as if his mother did not love him right now. Avni admits she cannot be sure.

qa.q: Why was asking "Can I have it on my birthday?" a wise move?
qa.a: It replaced screaming with a request, and it gave his mother something to say yes to. It also kept things calm between them.

qa.q: How might the shop scene look from Jomon's mother's side?
qa.a: She probably felt she had to hold the no, and was relieved and pleased when he chose to ask instead of scream.

grounding: My parent said no to the toy and I am furious; a wise child asks if he can have it on his birthday.
